Elections 

2026 General Election
 





 

 
The General Election will be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polls are open on Election Day from 7:00am to 8:00pm.
 
November 3, 2026
 General Election 
 

 A General Election is the election in which federal and state officers, members of Congress and of the general assembly, county and township officers, and other officers appear on the ballot. General Elections are held the 1st Tuesday after the 1st Monday in November of each even-numbered year. 

 
 

 
2026 General Election Calendar  

 

 Results will be posted on election night.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 


 
Voter Registration 
 

 
The Pre-Registration deadline for voter registration closes at 5pm Monday, October 19. Persons wishing to participate in this election who register to vote after October 19 will be required to provide proof of identification (i.e. current and valid photo identification card with an expiration date), AND proof of residency in their voting precinct, when they go to the polls on election day, or when they request an absentee ballot in-person. Other provisions may also apply. Persons not registered to vote by October 19, should expect a longer processing time at the polls on election day.

Absentee Voting 
 

 
Absentee Ballots: Wednesday, October 14 absentee ballots will be mailed and in-person voting starts in the Auditor's Office. 
 

Download an Absentee Ballot Request Form 
 
 
 
Tuesday, August 25 is the first day absentee ballot request forms will be accepted. 
 
Wednesday, October 14 is the first day absentee ballots will be mailed. 
 
Wednesday, October 14 is the first day to cast an absentee ballot in Auditor's Office. 
 
Monday, October 19 at 5pm is the deadline to request an absentee ballot by mail for this election. 
 
Monday, November 2  at 5pm is the deadline to vote an absentee ballot in Auditor's Office. 
 
Requests for absentee ballots must be in writing and should be mailed or delivered to: 
 
 
Cerro Gordo County Auditor, 220 N Washington Ave, Mason City IA 50401 
 
 
 
Find more information on Absentee Voting. 
 
 

All absentee ballots must be received by 8:00pm on Election Day to be considered on time to be counted. Postmarks no longer are acceptable.
